title: Sales Copilot
subtitle: Prepare cited account briefs, respect current CRM permissions and approve every consequential change.
theme: Agents and Copilots in Real Workflows
author: By Sourav Banerjee

practice_prompts.label: Workflow, outputs and risk boundary
practice_prompts.hint: Place the five outputs on read-only, draft-only and approved write-back, and list the questions that change the design.

practice_prompts.label: Three lanes and the two checks
practice_prompts.hint: Trace a question from SSO through the snapshot or route, the fresh post-check, the model and the claim verifier.

practice_prompts.label: Permissions and the territory change
practice_prompts.hint: Explain the CRM mirror, field masks, count leaks and what happens to a snapshot after a noon territory move.

practice_prompts.label: Failures, evaluation and the two pivots
practice_prompts.hint: Say what fails closed, which slices gate release, and how you answer the 30-45 s and model-regression drills.

rubric: Places summary/risks, questions/drafts and CRM updates on three distinct risk tiers before drawing components.
Builds the snapshot as the rep, keys it on account plus permission signature, and rechecks fresh attributes at serve time.
Treats a count or aggregate over another territory as a leak under the same zero-violation gate.
Routes counts and IDs to reviewed CRM operations and prose to hybrid search, and grounds risks in fetched fields with citations.
Blocks, not warns, on any external claim missing from the approved-claims playbook or pricing policy.
Requires exact-field preview, rep approval and an idempotency key for every CRM write.
Explains how 96.7% over 120 hid 83.3% on six regulated claims and adds independent critical-slice gates.
Answers the 30-45 s pivot by tracing first and bounding the agent graph, and measures adoption and prep time beside safety.

editorial_review.evidence: Re-read all 60 captured sections against the earlier draft and the rewrite. The draft had dropped the Sara/Acme trace, the guide's 'what it is really asking' examples, the weak/average/strong tiers, the stakeholder table, the explore list, the related-variants table, MoSCoW and the interview shortcut, the freshness-is-an-assumption caveat, the seven-step architecture and ENFORCE/APPROVE boundaries, the 'conversational coat' routing example, the warn-only-to-reduce-false-positives cause, the strong/weak incident answers, the sixty-second latency line and sub-3-second sibling, the two-minute answer, the eight lines, and the source group table; each is now restored in its step. The four lane/end-to-end figures had generic 'source figure N' captions; each now has a caption and paragraph read from its own labels. The draft's invented spoken answer was replaced by the source's two spoken answers, an empty table cell and broken abbr punctuation were fixed, and the authored territory exercise and two pivot reveals are labelled as additions. Cheat-sheet cards are recalled in Quick review only after full teaching. November 20 complete maintained-baseline review: Complete maintained casebook: eight walkthrough steps, six diagrams, source and field-permission maps, all three lanes, claim regression logs/scorecard, latency pivot, all practice answers and Quick review.
